summary: Wolfpen Mountain (Cagle) in Sequatchie County: the state's first fire tower site, a ca. 1933 CCC tower, then a steel Aeromotor LS-40 that stands today; sources disagree on height.

events.note: Ca. 1933 wood-frame Cagle tower built by the CCC; the Division's first fire tower per the National Register study
Visit report: cab locked; tower sign allowed visitors to climb at own risk; staffed only sometimes
Registered January 3, 2015 as US 1077, TN 19; nominated by Jerry Lutes

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives the original Cagle tower as 60 feet and the 1930s replacement as 80 feet. The National Register study gives the original as 50 feet. A 2006 visit report calls the current tower 100 feet. No height is recorded here.
The Register dates the replacement to the 1930s; the National Register study says the date is unknown.
The Register also calls it Cagle Tower, and a 2006 visit report notes a highway sign that called it Wolfpen Tower. Same site, two names.

sources.title: Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers, 1933 to 1975 (National Register multiple property document)

notes_for_editor: Current access is unverified: the only access evidence is a 2006 visit report (cab locked; a sign allowed climbing at own risk). Access key omitted rather than guessed. Staffing data is from 2006 only. Height is in conflict across 50, 60, 80 and 100 ft, so no height_m is set. Replacement date conflicts (1930s per Register, unknown per study). The record has no height_m and the NHLR elevation (2,252 ft) differs slightly from the record (686.4 m, which matches). Two searches and about six page reads used.
